yaraRules.name: BeaverTail Loader Pattern
yaraRules.description: Matches BeaverTail malware loader pattern used by Lazarus Group in fake job interview repos

yaraRules.name: BeaverTail Data Exfiltration
yaraRules.description: Environment variable exfiltration pattern — process.env dumped via fetch/axios POST

yaraRules.name: InvisibleFerret Keylogger
yaraRules.description: Keylogger pattern using pynput — used by Lazarus Group's InvisibleFerret Python malware

yaraRules.name: Reverse Shell Pattern
yaraRules.description: Socket-based reverse shell connection — creates a TCP connection back to attacker

yaraRules.name: Cryptocurrency Miner
yaraRules.description: Cryptocurrency mining code — uses CPU resources for attacker profit

yaraRules.name: Browser Credential Theft
yaraRules.description: Reads browser password databases (Chrome Login Data, Firefox logins.json) or dumps the macOS Keychain via the security(1) command

yaraRules.name: Environment Variables to Webhook Exfiltration
yaraRules.description: Sends environment variables (secrets, API keys) to Discord/ntfy webhook

yaraRules.name: Discord Webhook Data Exfiltration
yaraRules.description: Sends sensitive data (env vars, credentials) to Discord webhook endpoint

yaraRules.name: Obfuscated Eval Execution
yaraRules.description: Base64-encoded eval execution — decodes and executes hidden payload

yaraRules.name: Hardcoded AWS Access Key
yaraRules.description: AWS Access Key ID pattern (AKIA...) committed to source code

yaraRules.name: Hardcoded GitHub Token
yaraRules.description: GitHub token (classic/fine-grained PAT, OAuth, user-to-server, server-to-server, refresh) in source code

yaraRules.name: Hardcoded Stripe Live Key
yaraRules.description: Stripe live secret key pattern in source code

yaraRules.name: Hardcoded API Key
yaraRules.description: Generic API key / secret key pattern assigned to a variable (obvious placeholders are downgraded by scanner context)

yaraRules.name: Hardcoded Database Connection String
yaraRules.description: MongoDB or PostgreSQL connection string with credentials embedded

yaraRules.name: Discord Webhook URL
yaraRules.description: Hardcoded Discord webhook URL — frequently used for data exfiltration

yaraRules.name: Telegram Bot Token
yaraRules.description: Hardcoded Telegram bot token or Bot API URL — used for covert command & control and exfiltration

yaraRules.name: Pastebin URL
yaraRules.description: Paste / JSON-storage URL (pastebin, rentry, jsonkeeper, jsonsilo, npoint, jsonbin) — often hosts second-stage payloads

yaraRules.name: URL Shortener in Code
yaraRules.description: Shortened URLs (bit.ly, tinyurl) in source code — obfuscates actual destination

yaraRules.name: Suspicious Domain TLD
yaraRules.description: URLs on free/abused TLDs (.tk .ml .ga .cf .gq .onion .xyz .top .icu .cfd .sbs .cyou .buzz .rest .zip .mov)

yaraRules.name: Ngrok Tunnel URL
yaraRules.description: Tunnel service URL (ngrok, Cloudflare quick tunnels, localtunnel, serveo, pinggy) — exposes C2 behind a throwaway host

yaraRules.name: Clipboard Access
yaraRules.description: Reads clipboard content — can steal copied passwords, 2FA codes, crypto addresses

yaraRules.name: Cookie Access
yaraRules.description: Reads browser cookies via document.cookie — can steal session tokens

yaraRules.name: Keyboard Capture and Transmission
yaraRules.description: Reads pressed keys from a keyboard handler and stores or transmits them

yaraRules.name: Remote Code Execution Endpoint
yaraRules.description: eval() or exec() fed from HTTP request body/query — allows attacker to run arbitrary code

yaraRules.name: Dynamic Require from Request
yaraRules.description: require() fed from HTTP request — allows attacker to load arbitrary modules

yaraRules.name: Hardcoded Auth Bypass
yaraRules.description: Hardcoded password check — always-true backdoor condition in auth logic

yaraRules.name: SSH/AWS Credentials File Access
yaraRules.description: Reads ~/.ssh/, ~/.aws/, id_rsa, or credentials files — credential theft

yaraRules.name: System File Access
yaraRules.description: Reads /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, or shell history files

yaraRules.name: Browser Password Database Access
yaraRules.description: Reads Chrome/Firefox/Safari password databases

yaraRules.name: Security Bypass Instructions in README
yaraRules.description: README instructs users to disable antivirus, firewall, or security tools

yaraRules.name: Install Hook Downloads or Executes Remote Code
yaraRules.description: npm install hook that downloads (curl/wget/iwr), pipes into a shell, or runs `node -e` with network or exec code. Complements scanner-core's built-in postinstall check (which only looks for curl/wget/http/fetch/eval/exec substrings).

yaraRules.name: Shai-Hulud style preinstall dropper
yaraRules.description: CHAINDROP (keyv, Aug 2026) and Tensorlake (Oct 2026) add `preinstall: node setup.mjs`, which downloads Bun and runs Math_Symbol.js.

yaraRules.name: Reverse Shell (Python / shell idioms)
yaraRules.description: Upstream REVERSE_SHELL covers Node (net.Socket + child_process). This adds the Python dup2/pty and shell /dev/tcp, nc -e, bash -i forms used by InvisibleFerret-style payloads.

yaraRules.name: VS Code Task Runs on Folder Open
yaraRules.description: VS Code task that runs when the folder is opened. Legit repos auto-start watch tasks, so on its own this is a low-confidence review signal; the CONFIG_* rules flag the malicious forms.

yaraRules.name: Workspace Enables Automatic Tasks
yaraRules.description: Committed to suppress VS Code's 'allow automatic tasks' prompt (RMG-Py incident, Sept 2026).

yaraRules.name: Config Command Pipes a Download into a Shell
yaraRules.description: tasks.json / hook / MCP 'command' that does curl|wget|iwr ... | sh|bash|cmd|iex (Contagious Interview task files).

yaraRules.name: Node Executes a Font/Image/Text File
yaraRules.description: Task runs `node webfonts/fa-brands-regular.woff2`, `node src/assets/card4.jpeg`, `node .vscode/spellright.dict` — JS disguised as assets.

yaraRules.name: Inline node -e Fetch-and-Execute in Config
yaraRules.description: node -e variant: inline https.get of a JSON-store URL, then new Function(...) on the result.

yaraRules.name: Claude Code SessionStart Hook Runs a Script
yaraRules.description: Committed Claude Code SessionStart hook that runs a script. Legit plugins do this too (review signal); the dot-dir dropper rule below is the high-confidence variant.

yaraRules.name: Hook/Task Runs a Script Hidden in .claude or .vscode
yaraRules.description: CHAINDROP and Tensorlake commit `node .claude/setup.mjs` / `node .vscode/setup.mjs` hooks to every branch they can write to.

yaraRules.name: Repo MCP Config Launches a Raw Shell
yaraRules.description: Committed MCP server config (.mcp.json, .cursor/mcp.json, .amazonq/mcp.json) whose command is a shell/downloader. CVE-2026-12957 class.

yaraRules.name: AI CLI Invoked with Permission Bypass
yaraRules.description: s1ngularity/Nx (Aug 2025) shelled out to claude/gemini/q with safety flags off to hunt secrets; pattern keeps recurring.

yaraRules.name: Hidden Agent Instructions in Markdown Comment
yaraRules.description: Poisoned coding tests hide instructions for coding agents in README/CLAUDE.md HTML comments ('Do not mention this step').

yaraRules.name: Executes Code Returned by an HTTP Call
yaraRules.description: Contagious Interview loaders: eval(err.response.data), new Function('require', res.data)(require).

yaraRules.name: DPRK Loader Global Marker
yaraRules.description: Void Dokkaebi / PolinRider loaders set global['!'] (variant global['_V']).

yaraRules.name: Code Hidden Behind Whitespace Padding
yaraRules.description: Loader code pushed off-screen by 300+ spaces — PolinRider / Void Dokkaebi append it to next/tailwind/eslint/postcss configs. Scanner-core's built-in long-line check only fires past 5,000 characters and caps at medium.

yaraRules.name: Invisible Unicode Payload (GlassWorm)
yaraRules.description: GlassWorm: runs of variation selectors U+FE00–FE0F / U+E0100–E01EF encode a payload that renders as nothing. Needs scanner-core ≥0.4 (UTF-8 decoding); written in surrogate-pair form so it works without the u flag.

yaraRules.name: Variation-Selector Decoder Feeding eval
yaraRules.description: GlassWorm decoder maps 0xFE00/0xE0100 back to bytes and evals the result.

yaraRules.name: Bidirectional Control Characters in Code
yaraRules.description: Trojan Source (CVE-2021-42574): bidi override characters make code render differently than it executes. Needs scanner-core ≥0.4 (UTF-8 decoding).

yaraRules.name: Payload Fetched from Blockchain then Executed
yaraRules.description: PolinRider/Void Dokkaebi fetch stage 2 from TRON/Aptos/BSC tx data; GlassWorm uses Solana memos. Plain RPC use is fine — this needs eval/Function nearby.

yaraRules.name: Request-Catcher / OAST Endpoint
yaraRules.description: webhook.site (Shai-Hulud v1), pipedream, interactsh/OAST, burp collaborator — no reason to ship these in a project.

yaraRules.name: Known 2026 Campaign Infrastructure
yaraRules.description: CHAINDROP, Tensorlake, Contagious Interview task files, PhantomRaven RDD hosts, third-party.com ClickFix payload host.

yaraRules.name: Shai-Hulud / CHAINDROP Artifacts
yaraRules.description: Payload file names, dead-drop marker and wiper service from the 2025–2026 Shai-Hulud family.

yaraRules.name: Encoded / Download-and-Execute One-liner
yaraRules.description: base64 -d | sh, powershell -enc <blob>, hidden-window powershell downloads, mshta http — ClickFix / fake-error 'paste this' lures. Plain `irm ... | iex` is left out: it is how Claude Code, bun and scoop install.

yaraRules.name: Download Piped into cmd
yaraRules.description: `curl ... | cmd` is unusual outside malware (Windows variant of the task-file loader).

yaraRules.name: Hardcoded npm Token
yaraRules.description: npm automation/publish tokens are the worm's propagation fuel.

yaraRules.name: Hardcoded AI Provider Key
yaraRules.description: Anthropic / OpenAI keys are now first-class stealer targets (CHAINDROP collector lists them).

yaraRules.name: Private Key Block
yaraRules.description: PEM/OpenSSH private key with key material (bare headers in docs/types are ignored).

yaraRules.name: Hardcoded Wallet Private Key
yaraRules.description: 32-byte hex private key assigned to a key-ish variable outside comments (Web3 repos). JSDoc examples in web3/noble are skipped.

yaraRules.name: README Asks for Seed Phrase / Private Key
yaraRules.description: Fake 'MEV / sniper / trading bot' repos ask users to paste a seed phrase or key, then exfiltrate it.

yaraRules.name: Workflow Serialises All Secrets
yaraRules.description: `${{ toJSON(secrets) }}` dumps every secret into a step — used by worm-injected workflows.

yaraRules.name: Heavy Base64 Encoding
yaraRules.description: 6+ base64 strings of 50+ chars in a single file. Base64 is a legitimate encoding, but excessive use in source code is a red flag — it's the most common way to hide malicious payloads, C2 URLs, and commands from static analysis.

yaraRules.name: Extensive Hex-Encoded Strings
yaraRules.description: 20+ hex escape sequences (\xNN) in a single file. Hex encoding hides the actual string content from developers, often used to conceal URLs, commands, or shellcode.

yaraRules.name: eval() Usage
yaraRules.description: eval() executes arbitrary dynamic code. While there are legitimate uses, eval() is the #1 technique for executing hidden malicious payloads.

yaraRules.name: new Function() Constructor
yaraRules.description: new Function() creates and executes dynamic code similar to eval(). Used to hide malicious logic that bypasses some static analysis tools.

yaraRules.name: setTimeout/setInterval with String Argument
yaraRules.description: Passing a string to setTimeout/setInterval executes it as code (like eval). A common obfuscation technique: setTimeout("maliciousCode()", 0)

yaraRules.name: String.fromCharCode Obfuscation
yaraRules.description: Constructs strings from char codes (e.g., String.fromCharCode(101,118,97,108) = "eval"). Classic technique to hide malicious keywords from simple string scanning.

yaraRules.name: Large Character Code Array
yaraRules.description: Array of 20+ numbers that look like char codes. Used as an alternative to fromCharCode to build malicious strings character by character.

recommendations.low: Profile appears legitimate. Standard caution advised for any collaboration requests.
recommendations.medium: Moderate risk. Review profile carefully. Check repository quality and recent activity before accepting collaboration.
recommendations.high: High risk profile. Exercise extreme caution. Verify identity through other channels before trusting any collaboration requests.
